There were several years of analysis by NASA in the late 1960's regarding the follow-on steps after the Apollo missions to the moon. Saturn V was supposed to fly Apollos 18, 19, and 20 but Nixon killed the three flights after Apollo 13's nearly fatal accident.

By the time 1971 rolled around, the Apollo Applications program in full swing with Skylab the result.

Had STS been operational earlier, Skylab would have been capable of being reboosted and used as an early target.

Unfortunately, the scope and design of STS was drawn out and not fully completed until the mid-1970's.

The time between Apollo Soyuz and STS-1 is very similar to the time between the end of the Space Shuttle operations and the launch of CST or Orion.

However, the US federal spending on spaceflight has been inconsistent. The spending at NASA and USAF resulted in STS dependency for several years because until STS-51L, it was believed that STS was going to be the main route to and from LEO.
